prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian region airspace near capacity; airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. System: Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell), ATFM/A-CDM layer; doesn't replace ATC/airport/airline/handling ops. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone), Capacity Assessment Module (CAM), Slot Allocation Engine, Airport CDM Portal, Digital Briefing Room, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, Contingency Operations Console, Weather Ingest Gateway (WIG, Orchard), Flight Data Exchange, Surface Surveillance Adapter, Airline Interface Adapter, Alert Distribution Hub, Performance Analytics Warehouse, Audit Event Ledger, Identity Access Service, Business Rules Registry (BRR), Time Synchronization Service, Collaborative Decision Log, North/South Runway Meter, East/West Apron Sensor, Sector Load Monitor, Gate Conflict Detector, Common Situation Display. External (authenticated, audited): airline reservation, crew, baggage, commercial, national surveillance, avionics. Actors: Regional Flow Manager (RFM, Copperfin), Airline Operations Coordinator, Network Operations Liaison, Aircraft Operator Representative, Slot Coordinator, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Airport Duty Manager, Ground Handling Dispatcher, Handling Resource Planner, Deicing Coordinator, Meteorology Briefing Officer, Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison, Emergency Response Coordinator, Data Governance Steward, System Support Engineer. Items: Flight Intent Message (FIM), Airport Capacity Plan, Target Off Block Time, Calculated Takeoff Time, Airport Acceptance Rate (AAR), Tactical Regulation Proposal, Ground Delay Program status, Storm Cell Snapshot, Runway Inspection Note, Post Operations Report, forecast confidence record. Modes: Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, Slot Compliance State. Reqs: no binding CTTs in baseline; post-approval changes via controlled functions only; Metering/Arrival Console only under accountable roles, shown on Common Situation Display; escalate emergencies to Emergency Response Coordinator; Steward verifies Audit Event Ledger (synchronized timestamps); period-end data to Warehouse for Post Operations Report. Flows: Flight Data Exchange sends normalized FIM to Demand Prediction Service (FIM beats Airline Interface Adapter schedule). WIG validates weather feeds, marks late/invalid ones degraded (not excluded); Meteorology Briefing Officer reviews. CAM sends weather-adjusted values to Runway Meters, flags low-confidence capacity provisional; apron data correlated before Ramp Movement Board

New part:
S124: Airline Operations Centre integration provides the operational bridge between carrier recovery planning and the Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System.
S125: The Airline Operations Coordinator is known as Saffron in airline integration working sessions.
S126: Each airline operations centre submits a Flight Intent Message through the Airline Interface Adapter using an authenticated system account managed by the Identity Access Service.
S127: The Flight Intent Message includes the preferred route, requested departure timing, aircraft registration, turnaround status, crew readiness, and passenger connection sensitivity needed for flow assessment.
S128: The Airline Interface Adapter validates message structure, maps carrier codes to the Business Rules Registry, and forwards accepted intent data to the Flight Data Exchange.
S129: Invalid or incomplete intent submissions are rejected with machine-readable reasons so the Airline Operations Coordinator can correct them without informal voice coordination.
S130: Accepted intents are reflected on the Common Situation Display as proposed airline actions until the Regional Flow Platform reconciles them with airport and airspace constraints.
S131: The Demand Prediction Service uses current airline intents to refine departure demand, arrival demand, and recovery demand by time band.
S132: The Capacity Assessment Module compares that demand with the Airport Capacity Plan and the current Airport Acceptance Rate before recommending operating limits.
S133: The Capacity Assessment Module uses the Storm Cell Snapshot to qualify capacity confidence during convective weather impacts.
S134: The Slot Allocation Engine converts accepted constraints into Calculated Takeoff Time values and Target Off Block Time guidance for affected flights.
S135: Airline operations centres receive those constraints through the Airline Interface Adapter and may also view them in the Airport CDM Portal.
S136: When a Ground Delay Program is active, the Slot Coordinator reviews airline requests for priority handling against published equity and operational feasibility rules.
S137: Copperfin confirms airline recovery priorities before the Slot Allocation Engine publishes a revised constraint set.
S138: The Airline Operations Coordinator evaluates each constraint against crew legality, aircraft rotation continuity, maintenance positioning, and passenger recovery commitments.
S139: If the airline proposes a retime, cancellation, aircraft substitution, or route change, it submits an updated Flight Intent Message rather than relying on manual annotations.
S140: The Ground Handling Dispatcher sends the Crew Bus Delay Slip when crew transport lateness affects an aircraft turn.
S141: Ground handling impacts are correlated by the Handling Resource Planner with stand occupancy, baggage readiness, catering status, and boarding progress.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
